canonical_data: local project and global memory JSON under ~/.jcode/memory, with tags, relationships, categories, trust, sources, and superseded entries, recalled into named resumable sessions
current_repo_note: Reviewed at HEAD 1f612a7 (2026-10-14); the root LICENSE and the sdk/typescript/LICENSE are the same MIT blob. The managed cloud direction is documented as not yet deployed, so no cloud deployment is recorded.
strengths: Local JSON memory with tags, relationships, and superseded entries stays on the user's machine, ordinary telemetry carries no prompts or code, and transcript sharing is a separate opt-in program

Typed-relevance recall is tightly bounded: at most 24 memories per batch inside a 64 KiB budget, a 60-second deadline, fail-closed batches with no silent fallback, and credentials that cannot redirect
Provider breadth is documented per integration: named OAuth logins for Anthropic, OpenAI, and Gemini, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, self-hosted servers, and local models, plus MCP servers
Named resumable sessions on a persistent background server plus opt-in headless swarm workers give both interactive and background multi-session operation
weaknesses: The RAM and boot-time comparisons are vendor-measured against named tools with no independent reproduction, so the efficiency headline is a claim rather than a finding
Recall depends on external typed-decision endpoints in the default provider order whenever a Jcode login is configured; fully local recall needs explicit BYOK configuration
Subscription-gated memory decisions run through the vendor gateway with per-account entitlement checks, which the data-sovereignty reading counts against full self-sufficiency
677 open issues against nine months of history signal lively adoption and a substantial support burden at the same time
why_it_matters: A performance-obsessed coding harness that pairs a lean terminal agent with local memory and headless swarm sessions across many model providers.
